question: Who Owns Dunkin'?
quick_answer: Dunkin' is owned by Inspire Brands, a large US restaurant company that bought Dunkin' Brands in 2020 for about $11.3 billion and took it private. Inspire is backed by the private equity firm Roark Capital, and it also owns Baskin-Robbins, Arby's, Sonic, Buffalo Wild Wings and Jimmy John's. Dunkin' was founded in 1950 in Quincy, Massachusetts.

body.heading: Who owns Dunkin'?
body.text: Dunkin' is owned by Inspire Brands. In 2020, Inspire acquired Dunkin' Brands, the parent of both Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins, in a deal worth about $11.3 billion and took the company private. So Dunkin' no longer trades on the stock market.

body.heading: Backed by Roark Capital
body.text: Inspire Brands is backed by Roark Capital, an Atlanta-based private equity firm focused on restaurant and franchise businesses. Under Inspire, Dunkin' sits in a group that also includes Arby's, Sonic, Buffalo Wild Wings and Jimmy John's, as well as Baskin-Robbins.

body.heading: The brand's roots
body.text: Dunkin' was founded in 1950 in Quincy, Massachusetts, originally as Dunkin' Donuts. Over time it leaned more heavily into coffee and drinks and shortened its name to simply 'Dunkin'', though it is still known for its donuts and baked goods.

faqs.q: Is Dunkin' owned by the same company as Baskin-Robbins?
faqs.a: Yes. Both Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins are owned by Inspire Brands, which bought their shared parent, Dunkin' Brands, in 2020.
